**Answer: 807**

**Step 1: Reduce "short" to an order condition.** A rational number is short exactly when its reduced denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Write $N = cm$ and let $N'$ be the part of $N$ coprime to 10. Since $10^k-1$ is coprime to 10, $\frac{10^k-1}{N}$ is short if and only if $N' \mid 10^k-1$, i.e. $\operatorname{ord}_{N'}(10) \mid k$.

The set of $k\ge 1$ for which this holds is the set of multiples of $d=\operatorname{ord}_{N'}(10)$ (with $d=1$ when $N'=1$). So $t$ is $m$-tastic via $c$ exactly when $t=\operatorname{ord}_{(cm)'}(10)$. Therefore
$$S(m)=\{\operatorname{ord}_{(cm)'}(10) : 1\le c\le 2017\}.$$

**Step 2: Upper bound.** Since $(cm)' = m'\cdot c'$, where $c'$ is the prime-to-10 part of $c$, the value depends only on $c'$. Let
$$A=\{x\in[1,2017] : \gcd(x,10)=1\}.$$
Every $c'$ lies in $A$, so $|S(m)|\le |A|$. Counting, $1$–$2000$ contributes $800$ integers coprime to 10. In $2001$–$2017$ there are $4$ (from $2001,2003,2007,2009$) plus $3$ (from $2011,2013,2017$). So $|A| = 807$.

**Step 3: Construction attaining 807.** Let $P$ be the set of primes $p\le 2017$ with $p\ne 2,5$, and take
$$m=\prod_{p\in P} p^{J}$$
with $J$ large (say $J=20$). For $x\in A$, write $x=\prod p^{a_p}$, so $n_x = mx$ has $p$-exponent $J+a_p$.

For a prime power $q^e$ with $q\ne 2,5$, $\operatorname{ord}_{q^e}(10)=\operatorname{ord}_q(10)\cdot q^{\,e-f_q}$ for $e\ge f_q$, where $f_q$ is a fixed small constant. Here $\operatorname{ord}_q(10)\mid q-1$, so it contributes no factor of $q$, and its other prime factors are at most $2016$ in size. The $q$-part of $\operatorname{ord}_{mx}(10)$ is therefore $q^{\,J+a_q-f_q}$ (the other contributions have $q$-exponent at most $\log_q 2016$, which is far below $J$). Because the $q$-exponent of the order recovers $a_q$ for every $q\in P$, the map $x\mapsto \operatorname{ord}_{mx}(10)$ is injective on $A$.

Hence $|S(m)|=807$ for this $m$.

Combining the two bounds, the maximum is $807$.

ANSWER: 807
